Screening Menus

A seller lays out a menu, and buyers pick for themselves.

The seller cannot tell big spenders from small ones. So the menu offers two sizes. The big option is made in full. The small option is shrunk on purpose. Shrinking it stops big spenders from lying. In return, big spenders pocket a bonus called information rent. The formulas below set the two sizes.

For example, a 🏪 shop sells 🍬 candy in a big 📦 box and a small box. Big spenders choose the big box. The small box is made tiny on purpose. Pretending to be a small buyer would only hurt. So big spenders honestly pick the big box.
